title: Play tabletop pinball: launch the ball, then flip it back up into the top lanes
instruction: Play the pinball machine: launch the ball with the plunger, then flip it back up into the top lanes with a flipper.
context: Pinball is a familiar arcade and bar game. Even one good shot takes two kinds of control: drawing the spring plunger back far enough that the ball makes it up the lane and round the top, then pressing the flipper button at the moment the ball rolls onto the flipper, so it is struck back up the playfield instead of draining between the flippers. The ball is in play for about two and a half seconds between launch and flipper, and the hand has to get from the plunger to the button in that time.
setup: Station table; x forward from the line through the arm bases, y to the robot's left of their midpoint (bases at y +/-30.5 cm), heights from the table top. (1) A tabletop pinball machine of the EastPoint Sports arcade type (moulded cabinet 483 mm deep along x, 330 mm wide, its front toward the robot at x 20.0 cm, centred on y 0, held to the table by its feet and two padded clamps so it cannot move). Its yellow playfield (420 x 306 mm) starts 50 mm behind the front panel and rises 6 degrees away from the robot between the cabinet's side panels (125 mm tall); a 50 mm deep front deck, 100 mm tall, spans the front. Along the right wall runs a 26 mm plunger lane, 330 mm long, with a curved guide at the top right turning the ball across the top; red inlane guides run from the side walls down to two white flippers (60 mm long, 12 mm thick, 18 mm tall) pivoting 75 mm up the playfield and 68 mm either side of its centre line, their tips angled 28 degrees down toward a 30 mm drain gap; each flips up 56 degrees. A white line across the playfield 330 mm up marks the top lanes, with two short dividers. The plunger: a red knob (26 mm across, 22 mm long) on a shaft standing 35 mm out of the front panel, 48 mm above the table, in line with the lane (y -14.0 cm); drawn back up to 45 mm against its spring. The flipper buttons: two yellow buttons (22 mm across) on the front deck's top, 25 mm behind the front panel at its left and right corners (y +/-14.3 cm), pressing down 6 mm; past 3.5 mm a button fires its flipper. (2) A 19 mm steel ball resting in the plunger lane against the plunger's tip. Both grippers open at the ready pose.
scoring: Positions are read along the playfield's slope (u, from the playfield's front edge) and across it. Launched: the ball has left the plunger lane for the playfield. Flipped: after the ball has left the plunger lane, it is struck by a flipper: it moves up the slope faster than 0.3 m/s while that flipper is raised more than half way, having been within that flipper's reach (82 mm of its pivot: its length, the ball's radius and 12 mm) in the last 0.2 s, and within 0.3 s after that flipper fired. A launch with a flipper up, or a bounce off a flipper held up, is not a shot. Top: after a flipper shot, the ball reaches the top lanes' line, 330 mm up. Drained: the ball falls between or past the flippers to within 30 mm of the bottom; nothing after that counts. Hand in the game: a gripper over the playfield inside the cabinet's walls (a run with one scores 0). 1.0: a flipper shot into the top lanes. 0.5: a flipper shot that does not reach them. 0.25: launched, never flipped. 0: not launched, and any hand in the game. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. Success: 1.0 held for 1 s. Real trial: a phone held overhead (looking straight down on the playfield, 60 fps) films the run; the top lanes' line is printed on the playfield and a tape line marks 30 mm (the drain line), so the strike, the ball's direction and the crossings are read off the video frame by frame.
reset_notes: Ball back in the plunger lane against the plunger; both flippers down; buttons up. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid cabinet, flippers and steel ball. The machine's playfield layout, flipper size and travel, plunger travel and spring (300 N/m), button travel and the frictions are estimates for the named type. One rule stands in for each flipper's switch and coil: a button pressed past 3.5 mm drives its flipper up through a stiff spring.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (800 steps, the run limit); demo: 1.0 (scripted, success at step 215)
